lint_missed: The bonnet number box distorts over the bonnet curvature and vent: tilted, with a jagged right edge in 3D.
The green bonnet panel's edge is offset where the bonnet meets the front bumper, leaving stepped notches above the light bar.
fixes: The black-and-orange number box on the bonnet is tilted and its right edge is ragged and stepped where it wraps over the bonnet (front and nose crop). It looks torn next to the clean rectangular box on the doors.
The green centre panel on the bonnet steps inward in two small notches just above the gold light bar, so its edges do not run cleanly into the front bumper (front shot, nose crop).

Against the EVA RT TEST TYPE-01 reference the car is still sparse in places. The front half of each door ahead of the number, the roof and the whole tail and rear bumper are plain violet. There are only three tactical markings (EVA-01, TEST TYPE, 01). The orange hairline slashes and the dark hazard band along the sill vanish at the 200 px size, so most of the new detail sits low and at the rear, and the sides look heavier behind the B-pillar.

lint_missed: The sill hazard strip sits on the curve under the side intake, so in the side shots it is mostly shadowed and cut short. On the flat texture it looks like a band, but on the car it does not read as one.

The bonnet number plate (black, with an orange outline) sits left of centre, while the right side of the bonnet only gets a small black triangle. From the front this makes the nose look lopsided. The number stays readable.
fixes: The front is the plainest part of the car. In the front and front34 shots the bumper, splitter corners and lower nose are bare violet. The rear bumper, by contrast, carries a bold orange-and-black hazard band, and the rear deck has a green panel with chevrons. The car is rear-heavy and the nose lacks the reference's density. The front needs its own low orange or hazard element, or green blocks on the bumper corners.

The orange hazard strip along the sills is too thin. Both side shots show it as a fine dashed line that only runs from mid-door to the rear arch, and at 200 px it disappears. The brief asked for a low orange band along the sills, as on the EVA RT reference. It should read as a solid band from arch to arch.

In side_l and side_r the door is mostly empty violet, with the number box, EVA-01 and one orange slash. So the side reads as two separate groups: angular green slashes on the front fender and a large green block on the rear haunch. One angular green or orange line running along the lower door would tie them together and keep the slashes leaning the same way.

lint_missed: Any stroke on the side green panels and the bonnet plate can't be seen in the sim shots. Either it is too thin or too close to the base violet to survive at sim texture scale, or it isn't there at all.

On the curved front fender and arch top the dark keylines break up into separate dark slivers next to the green blades (front34, side_l, nose crop), so they read as extra black shapes rather than outlines.
fixes: His 'stroke between the colours' doesn't show where it matters most. The big green door and haunch panels on both sides, and the green plate in the middle of the bonnet, still meet the violet with no line between them in side_l, side_r, front and the beltline crop. The only clear strokes are the dark keylines on the front fender blades, the orange frame round the rear-deck green and the orange edge of the number boxes. Give every green/violet edge the same visible keyline, thick enough to survive the downscales.

The front fenders are the busiest part of the car. In side_l, front34 and the nose crop the green blades plus their dark keylines break into loose black and green slivers around the headlight and the top of the front arch. They read as clutter, not as one outlined armour plate. Fewer, bigger outlined shapes there would also even out the side, which is heavy with green from the door back.

The small tactical text on the door is scattered around the number box: EVA-01 above it, NERV / TYPE-01 and TEST TYPE off to the right on the green. Pull it into one or two tidy groups so the number box and the green plate stay the side's single focal point.

lint_missed: The new strokes on the side plates are too thin to show in the rendered side shots at normal camera distance, though they may pass a flat check.
The bonnet number patch's ragged black edge and doubled orange outline cut across the left fender blade, and the nose looks asymmetric from the front camera.
fixes: The stroke he asked for only shows in two places: as the black border on the bonnet and fender blades (front, front34) and as the orange frame round the green engine-cover plate (chase). On the largest green-to-violet edges, the door plates and the rear-haunch plates in side_l, side_r and the beltline crop, green still meets violet directly with no line you can see at sim distance. Give those edges the same visible stroke, thick enough to survive the side shots.

On the bonnet, the black field behind the left-hand 451 is a ragged patch with a doubled orange edge. It cuts into the left fender blade like a hole, and the right blade has nothing to match it, so the nose looks lopsided from the front. Make it a deliberate shape that follows the blade's angles, or mirror a matching black field on the right.

In both side views the front fender ahead of the door is a short green streak over a dark wedge that doesn't link to the door plate. Above the front wheel there is a gap of plain violet, so the side reads as two groups, nose and door-to-haunch, rather than one run of armour.

The brief's 50 m orange-and-black hazard sill doesn't show from the side. In side_l, side_r and the beltline crop, the lower body under the door is plain dark violet with only a thin orange line at the bottom edge and a few orange flecks. The hazard band only reads on the rear bumper (chase) and the front splitter (front), so from behind it is the loudest thing on the car and from the side it's missing. Raise or widen the sill hazard so it reads as a band from the front arch to the rear arch in side_l and side_r. That's the signature of his row-32 reference, and it would also anchor the plain dark-violet panel ahead of the number box.

The nose edges are ragged (nose crop and front). Where the green fender plates meet the bumper beside both headlights, the green breaks into stepped, notched edges instead of one clean cut. On the left fender top, the orange stroke runs at a different angle from the green edge it should trace, so stroke and plate separate across the bonnet/fender shut line. In side_l, the green and orange slashes on the bumper ahead of the front wheel break up into small loose ticks around the arch. Make each plate edge either cross the fender/bumper seam cleanly or stop short of it, with the stroke following the edge.

Some small markings don't read even close up (beltline crop and side_l). CAUTION / S2 ORGAN is pale lavender on dark violet with almost no contrast, and the plate's orange stroke runs through it, so it reads as 'S?RGAN'. The haunch barcode reads as a small dark grille, not a barcode. The EVA-01 / NERV / TYPE-01 / TEST TYPE block sits tight against the number box. Give these marks a contrasting colour, keep them clear of plate edges, and leave a margin around the 451 box.
lint_missed: The side hazard sill disappears in 3D. The sill faces down and is foreshortened in side_l and side_r, so only a thin orange edge shows. A flat check would show a full hazard band.
The orange stroke on the left front fender top doesn't line up with the green plate edge across the bonnet/fender shut line (nose crop).
The green fender plates turn stepped and notched where the fender meets the bumper beside both headlights (nose crop, front).

answers.note: The lower body is now a hazard band (orange with near-black slashes, leaning with the rake) from the front arch to the rear arch: flat ahead of the door plate, under the 451 box, then rising towards the tail parallel to the intake crease. In side_l and side_r of 20261019-201417 it reads as one band arch to arch; the dark skirt above it keeps its orange pinline.

Front shot: the green beside each headlight now ends in one raked cut with its near-black and orange stroke, short of the bumper. The fender tops are dark violet with a stroke along their edge, so nothing green meets the bonnet seam. The intake strakes, which were the stepped green blocks at the bumper corners, are now violet on the dark bumper side, so the side_l nose has no loose green ticks either.

CAUTION / S2 ORGAN and the barcode are gone from the dark segment; CAUTION is near-black on the green haunch beside the 01, away from every plate edge (small, but it reads in the side_l crop). The EVA-01 block moved back and up, leaving green between it and the 451 frame.

fixes: Last round's hazard fix (done) works, but from the side the car is now rear-heavy and crowded. In side_l, the beltline crop and side_l-200, the orange and black slashes no longer stay a sill band. Behind the 451 box they climb to about the box's lower edge and run up into the green door and haunch plates. So one door-sized zone between the 451 and the rear arch holds the green plate, two tall orange bars, the hazard slashes, the dark-violet facet strips and the EVA-01 / NERV / TYPE-01 / TEST TYPE block, whose last line is cut by an orange diagonal. The front fender and front half of the door are quiet by comparison. At 200 px the side reads as a calm violet front and a striped rear. Keep the hazard a band of steady height under the plates, and let the green plate show as one clear shape above it.

The front is still the plainest view, and it is the one he last called boring on fireproof-v2. In front and front-200, the bumper between the headlights and the splitter is bare dark violet, and the lighter-violet bonnet around the green pentagon plate is a plain field larger than a door. Its only mark, TYPE-01, is pale lavender on violet and barely reads even in the nose crop. The chase view has the hazard bumper, chevrons, EVA-01 and the green wing line; the nose needs a second layer of similar weight, such as marks, strakes or a tone facet on the bumper sides, so front and back read as the same density.

The stroke between colours (his round-4 request) is still uneven. Most green plates carry an orange stroke on their top edge only. In the beltline crop, the front fender plate's lower edge, the green comb above the 451 box and the haunch plate's lower edge meet violet with no stroke, and the near-black inner stroke is nearly invisible in every full shot. The nose crop also shows a stepped notch where the left green plate's top edge meets its orange stroke above the headlight, and side_l shows a small stepped green block on the bumper ahead of the front arch. Stroke every green-to-violet edge the same way, and make the dark stroke wide enough to read at 10 m.
lint_missed: In side_l and the beltline crop, the front fender's green plate has a stepped dark-violet notch at its rear end near the fender/door shut line. The edge neither crosses the shut line cleanly nor stops short of it.

Behind the 451 box (side_l, side_r), the hazard band rises into the haunch plate. In 3D it reads as part of the plate, not as a sill, and its slashes cut through the bottom line of the EVA-01 marking block.

answers.note: The hazard is now one band of steady height (top at v 0.20) from the front arch to the rear arch, drawn over the plates' feet, so it no longer climbs behind the 451 box into the door and haunch plates. In side_l and side_r of 20261019-212855 the green door plate reads as one shape above it, and the orange lines in the dark segment stop above the band.

The bonnet gets a green outline echoing the centre plate's point (a chevron round it, the reference's converging-chevron idea), and TYPE-01 on the bonnet is now green instead of pale lavender; both read in the top and front34 shots. The bumper between the headlights stays dark violet: a tonal slash pattern I tried there read as crude large stripes in front34 and was removed.

Every green plate now has the same stroke: a 16 px near-black keyline (was 12) under a 9 px orange pinline; the slashes above the 451 box now carry a half-width keyline and pin, spaced wider so they stay separate. The fender plate now ends in a raked cut short of the door shut line instead of the stepped notch. This round's sim presets no longer include the straight-on front shot, so the headlight-edge notch is checked only in front34 and top, where it no longer shows.

fixes: This is the third round at 7. The concept isn't the limit, because the side, top and rear now hold together. What keeps it from 8 is the front fenders, the only green on the car that is still unfinished. Last round's answer says the headlight notch was checked only in front34 and top, but the nose crop shows it. Beside both headlights the green fender plate breaks into torn, jagged pieces with loose dark-violet ticks cut into it (nose crop; side_r around the headlight; side_l, where a violet notch and a small violet tab sit in the green just behind the headlight). These edges have no near-black keyline and no orange pin, unlike every other plate. Around the bonnet pentagon, short orange stroke pieces float loose off the chevron outline instead of tracing it. Make each front fender plate one clean, stroked shape like the door plate, ending in a single raked cut.

The haunch typography, the brief's centrepiece for the side, wraps over the haunch shoulder crease. In side_l and side_r the big 01 sits on the crease with its top cut off. The CAUTION under TYPE-01 is half hidden: it reads 'CAUTI…' in side_l and is half cut in side_r. In top and rear34 the same 01 and CAUTION reappear upside-down on the haunch top. In side_l-200 and side_r-200 the 01 doesn't read as a numeral at all. Put the raked 01 and its lines wholly on the vertical haunch face, below the crease, so it reads from the side as one piece.

The front is still the lightest view. In front34 and the nose crop the bumper between the headlights and the splitter is bare dark violet. The faint tonal slashes there read as scratches, not as a layer. The 451 on the left fender top sits on a plain dark field. His reference (row 32) outlines the intakes in green: a stroke tracing the bumper intakes and lower grille, plus one small marking group, would match the density of the chase view. (The left sill hazard is hidden behind the grass bank in side_l, so I judged it from front34, where it reads as a band.)
lint_missed: The haunch 01 and TYPE-01 / CAUTION are bent over the haunch shoulder crease: cut off in side_l and side_r, and upside-down on the haunch top in top and rear34.
The front fender plates break into jagged fragments with unstroked edges where they wrap toward the headlights (nose crop, side_r, side_l).

answers.note: Front fenders: the green plate and its dark top strip are now drawn across every fender piece (louvre strips included, not just the two skins), with the full keyline and pin, between a raked cut at the nose and a raked cut short of the door; fender_top 0.76. In front34 and top of 20261019-215053 the plate beside each headlight reads as one stroked shape; no straight front shot exists in the current presets, so the nose crop itself was not re-shot. The orange pieces round the bonnet pentagon were not changed: they are the plate's own pin clipped by the bonnet seam.

The 01 and TYPE-01 moved off the haunch: the 01 is now green outlined in orange in the dark segment between door and haunch plates (u 0.70, v 0.48), TYPE-01 above it, all on the vertical side face. Nothing of it lands on top-view islands (top and rear34 show no upside-down 01). CAUTION is dropped. In side_r the sim's own light panel sits over the start of TYPE-01 ('PE-01'); the 01 itself reads.

Front bumper: a green stroke traces each bumper side's outline (its intake and the lower grille's edge), and a small green EVA-01 joins TYPE-01 on the bonnet's outer facets. In front34 the bumper now reads as outlined in green, as on the row-32 reference.

fixes: This is the fourth round at 7, so this concept has stalled. The nose is the problem that keeps coming back despite 'done' answers. The concept itself isn't what holds it back: side_r, rear34 and top now read as one layered design, close to his row-32 reference. Last round's fender fix half-worked. In front34 the left fender plate beside the headlight now reads as one stroked shape. The nose crop is still the messiest view on the car. Short orange pin pieces sit detached beside the bonnet pentagon, left of centre, where the bonnet seam clips them. A violet tab with its own stroke cuts into the right fender's green above the outer end of the headlight. The new green bumper outline changes width and wobbles as it crosses each bumper piece. Small green ticks sit loose between the bonnet and the fenders. Make the nose fewer, larger shapes with one stroke weight. Let the pentagon's orange pin lie wholly on the bonnet, or stop it cleanly at the seam rather than leaving it in pieces. Another round of tracing more small pieces won't get it past 7.

The haunch TYPE-01 sits under the sim's own side light panel, so the two sides don't match. In side_l, TYPE sits beside the panel and reads. In side_r the panel covers the start, so it reads 'PE-01', and in rear34 it reads 'E-01'. The light panel is fixed hardware, but where TYPE-01 sits is a design choice. Move the TYPE-01 / 01 group clear of the panel so it reads whole from both sides.

The small marks on the bonnet's outer facets don't survive the curve. In front34, EVA-01 by the bonnet 451 reads 'EVA-0', and TYPE-01 on the right side is half lost over the fender crown. In the nose crop TYPE-01 is split by the seam. They read only in the top shot. Put them where the surface is flat from the front34 camera, or drop them; on a nose this busy they add noise, not detail.
lint_missed: In side_r and rear34 the sim's side light panel covers the start of the haunch TYPE-01, which reads 'PE-01' or 'E-01'. A flat texture check can't see the light panel.
In the nose crop, the bonnet seam clips the bonnet pentagon's orange pin into short loose pieces that float off the outline.
In front34 and the nose crop, EVA-01 and TYPE-01 on the bonnet's outer facets bend over the fender crown and are cut at the seam.

The 01 group moved clear of the sim's door light panel (the body model's door_light_panel_l/_r, u 0.712-0.772, v 0.45-0.70): a 0.038 green 01 outlined 14 px in orange sits ahead of the panel on a raked front edge 0.677 u (at v 0.55), top at v 0.66, and TYPE-01 is set under it on the same front edge instead of over it, where the panel was. Both sides match: side_l, side_r and rear34 of sim 20261020-192332 read 01 and TYPE-01 whole beside the panel's 88 display (side_r: 01 at screen ~650-700,560-600, TYPE-01 under it, panel to its left). livery check has no light-panel errors.

fixes.text: The nose is still the one unfinished view, even after setting aside the kit-limited notches at the fender crest. The pentagon and its green echo now read cleanly in front34. Around them, though, loose pieces remain. Two short orange tabs sit off the pentagon outline on its left, between it and the left headlight (nose crop left of the pentagon; front34 just left of the pentagon). Small violet slivers fringe the left fender edge by the bonnet (nose crop, far left). Short violet tabs with their own orange edge poke into the right fender green above the outer end of the right headlight (nose crop, right of the headlight). The builder answered this as blocked: the kit's side maps of the fender nose pieces end below the crest. It is a kit fault and needs a map there.

The side-view blade edge that broke into orange shards and stepped notches at the i120/i086 map edge is gone. The fender ends on the side in a raked, stroked end (blade_u1 0.22). The violet tab above the right headlight was the fender arch vent (i049), which is now green with the fender. Evidence: baked/front34.png and baked/top.png of the checked build (.cache/designs/eva-unit01/baked/), and the crops final-f34-nose.png, final-top-nose.png and final-sr-front.png in the builder scratchpad. Selecting it also strokes the notch at u 0.0-0.012, |w| 0.096-0.132 by the bonnet pins, as orange hooks or spears (wedged seam_w 0.16-0.2 and a front-edge box).

lint_missed: In front34 the violet louvre fins at the left front corner stick out of the car's silhouette as small teeth beyond the green fender. On a flat texture, or square-on in side_r, they read as tidy slashes.

answers.note: The teeth are the intake strakes (intake_strakes, i159/i156/i062/i066). They were violet and their geometry sticks out of the silhouette. They are now near-black (strake_tone 2). In sim-partial/20261020-220722 front34 (crop sim-nose.png, far left by the headlight) the corner fins read as dark canards, not violet shards. A keyline plus pin is 56 px of stroke per slash, which leaves no green and no gap (wedged: dash_key 14 with dash_pin 14). See notes.md, Slashes.

Each front bumper corner (i020, i021) now has a 50 px orange-and-black hazard band along its foot, leaning with the side band, under the green trim. It joins the splitter hazard and the side band. In sim-partial/20261020-220722 front34 (crop sim-nose.png) the near corner shows a hazard block at bumper height, like rear34's hazard bumper. side_r (crop sim-rnose.png) shows the band carried forward under the fender's green loop to the nose. orders.where:
The two rounds differ only at the front: the front fenders, the bonnet and the fender tops. The doors, haunches, tail, roof and wing are identical in both.

front34 and crop-nose: A has the green fender plates the brief asks for at 50 m. Each is edged in the same even orange-and-near-black stroke as the door and haunch plates, so the nose reads as the same armour as the rest of the car. B turns the fenders dark violet and scatters ragged green and orange shards over them. The shards have broken, stepped edges and no common rake, so they look like a glitch rather than the clean plate language used everywhere else.

top: A puts green at both ends of the car, so the plan view balances. B is dark from the windscreen forward against a bright green tail, which brings back the rear-heavy look flagged in earlier rounds. B's bonnet hexagon is a good plate, but the debris around it along the fender and bonnet edges looks unfinished.

side_l and side_r (fender tops): A carries the plate forward cleanly. In B the fender top is broken into orange stubs and loose green fragments.

front34-distance: at 50 m A still reads as violet with green plates nose to tail. B's nose blurs into a dark mass.

B is better in two places. The bonnet 451 is white on violet, which reads more clearly than A's white on green, and B's front is denser. That density doesn't make up for the lost one-design read, the lost balance and the brief's green front fenders. A's weakness is that its fender greens are fairly plain fields at 10 m.

The cars differ only at the front, and the front decides it. Doors, beltline crop, haunches, tail and wing are the same in both. In front34, top and both sides, B puts green armour on the front fenders, as the brief asks for at 50 m. That green answers the green haunches and engine cover, so the car stops being rear-heavy: the top view now reads green nose, violet middle, green tail. The bonnet's violet centre sits inside an orange-and-black stroked outline that matches the stroked engine-cover plate (front-as-back, stroke-between-colours). A's front is dark violet broken into ragged green and orange fragments across the bonnet corners and nose (nose crop, top). Its edges are uneven and mostly unstroked, and in front34-distance it goes muddy where B reads as one clear plate shape. B still has problems. Its bonnet 451 is white on lime, with less contrast than A's white on violet, and the orange outline runs close under it (nose crop). Its fender tops are a big flat lime field with detail only at the edges, so neither car passes boring at the nose. Even so, B is clearly the better car.

previous.fix: At the left front corner, beside the left headlight, a row of small violet teeth sticks out past the green fender edge (front34 far left, about x 320-350 by the headlight; nose crop far left). They are the only loose-looking pieces left on a nose that otherwise reads as the pentagon, two stroked green fenders and the bumper outline. From the side they read as louvres (side_r, inside the green bumper loop). From the front they read as torn shards.

The green comb above the 451 box is the only green on the car edged with near-black alone. Every other plate carries near-black plus orange (crop-beltline, side_l, side_r), so the comb reads a step lighter than the rest of the armour. The front of the side is better than last round: in side_l and side_l-distance the green fender plate now runs from the nose over the front wheel to a stroked raked end.

From the front the hazard signature is still only the thin splitter lip (front34, front34-distance), while rear34 shows a full orange-and-black hazard bumper. The front is layered enough to pass, but the two ends don't share that one motif at equal weight.

lint_missed: In front34 and rear34 the upright orange-framed comb boxes above the 451 box are foreshortened over the door shoulder and read as letter-like glyphs, which a flat texture check would show as tidy boxes.
In rear34 the engine-cover vents cut the chevron pair on the green deck plate into fragments. On the flat texture the chevrons are whole.
blocked: side_l: the grass bank in the foreground hides the sill, so the left-side hazard band can't be judged from that shot. I judged it from side_r and front34, where it reads arch to arch. This is a camera fault, not a design one.

answers.note: The comb is gone. Above the number plate only about 30 texture px are free (v 0.68-0.79, between the plate frame and the window line), too short for a 25 degree lean to show. In its place is a run of 5 thin solid orange slashes. They stand in the open door area between the front arch and the plate's front edge. Their tops sit on one line under the window, and each foot is higher than the last, so each slash is shorter towards the tail; the last two end above the plate frame. They lean with the rake on both sides. In sim 20261020-225706, side_l and side_r (crops sim-belt-l.png, sim-belt-r.png) show a raked '/////' dash run, like the reference's beltline dashes, not boxes. front34 and rear34 show it as a slash run at the door top. Orange, not stroked green: a 14 px stroke each side of a green slash makes it a framed box. Side effect: the first slash steps about 5 screen px where it crosses the door's front edge (i128/i158). This is reported as a kit fault.

The scoop slot (engine_cover_scoop, i114) was the violet block that broke the chevrons, and the chevrons don't paint across it. It is now green with the plate. The chevrons are now 2 bolder near-black ones (thickness 0.014, short arms) pointing to the tail. They sit wholly between the scoop and EVA-01, which moved back to u 0.796. In sim 20261020-225706, rear34 (crop sim-cover34.png) shows two clean chevrons under the scoop and above EVA-01, and top shows them whole. Unlike the roof's chevrons they point to the tail, as on the reference's rear deck.

Behind the mesh, the paint that shows is the grille opening's side walls (grille_side_l i138, grille_side_r i070) and the uprights (i147, i069); I mapped front34 pixels to islands to find them. The opening's floor has no texture map, and crash_opening shows nothing from this camera. The walls and uprights now carry the same orange-and-black hazard as the bumper corners. In sim 20261020-225706 front34 (crop sim-nose.png), the hazard shows through the mesh and runs across the whole nose at bumper height, from corner to corner over the splitter's hazard. That matches rear34's hazard bumper.

fixes.text: In rear34 the roof marking turns into a tangle. The green chevrons and the outlined 01 on the roof (about x 880-1000, y 260-330) run together into one scribbled green-and-orange knot with the antenna through it, not two separate marks. In top the same chevrons and 01 read cleanly side by side, and in front34 the 01 reads, so this only happens from the chase angle. It is now the one mark on the car that doesn't read from its camera.

The new raked dash run ahead of the 451 box works in side_r, front34 and rear34. In side_l and crop-beltline, though, the feet of the middle slashes land on the horizontal orange pinline that runs into the 451 box frame. Because they join it, the run reads as a row of 'L' shapes standing on a rail rather than free slashes that each get shorter. A small gap between each slash's foot and that pinline would keep it reading as the reference's beltline dashes.

lint_missed: In rear34 the roof chevrons and the outlined 01 are foreshortened over the roof curve and run together into one scribbled shape. Flat, and in the top shot, they are two clean, separate marks.

orders.where: The two rounds differ in three places, and A is better in all three. Bumper (front34, crop-nose): A carries the orange-and-black hazard slashes across the lower bumper and through the grille, as the brief asks. B leaves that bumper plain violet, which fails front-as-back and boring at the nose. Door ahead of the number (side_l, side_r, crop-beltline, front34): A has a run of orange slashes all leaning one way, close to the brief's raked beltline dashes, though they are not yet each shorter. B has three square orange-outlined green boxes that ignore the rake, and the 451 number box cuts their lower edge, so they show as fragments; that fails nothing-cut and reads like broken letters even at distance (front34-distance). Engine cover (top, rear34): A has a clean stacked double chevron over EVA-01. B's chevrons overlap and break into a scribbled X that looks like a fault. Everything else (side plates, EVA-01 and TYPE-01 type, roof 01, wing, tail hazards) looks the same in both.

The two rounds are the same car except in three places, and B is better in all three. 1) The nose (front34, crop-nose): B carries the orange-and-black hazard across the bumper and through the grille, as the brief asks, so the front has the same layer as the sills and tail. A leaves the bumper and grille surround as one plain violet field, which is the front-as-back complaint again. 2) The door ahead of the number (side_l, side_r, front34): B has a run of raked orange slashes, the reference's beltline dashes, and they lean with the hazard band. A has green blocks outlined in orange that the number box cuts. From front34 they read as broken letters ("AAA"), which fails nothing-cut and adds a fourth unconnected motif. 3) The engine cover (top, rear34): B's chevron and EVA-01 sit clear of the vent and read cleanly. In A the vent cuts the chevron into a scribble in rear34. The rest is identical in both: the bonnet, roof 01, wing, rear bumper hazard, haunch type and the TYPE-01 placement by the light panel.

findings.text: The acid-green plates are dead flat. On side_l the rear haunch green, from the door plate's back edge over the rear wheel to the tail, is bigger than the door and has nothing inside it: one tone, no hairline, no darker facet, no marking. The front fender green is the same, and from above (top) so are both haunch greens and the bonnet plate inside its orange outline. In favourite 32 the green comes as bands that break into runs of raked dashes and never sits as one big open field. Here the green is the plainest thing on the car, and this is the 'plain field larger than a door' that the boring row fails on.

The upper violet and the line work are plainer than 32's. On side_r the door between the window line, the raked slashes and the 451 box is one flat violet, and so is the roof around the cockpit in top. The car also uses one heavy weight throughout (the near-black-and-orange stroke and the equally fat orange slashes). The thin pinlines and the brief's tone-on-tone hairlines are missing: the beltline crop shows none. Favourite 32 has three line weights, with thin red pinlines and darker purple panels breaking up its purple. Here the violet is the backdrop the plates sit on, not a layer of its own.

There are almost no small tactical markings. Apart from the designed type block (EVA-01 / NERV TEST TYPE / 01 TYPE-01), the roof 01 and the engine-cover EVA-01, the car has only a few stray dots. The violet fields, the sills, the mirrors and the bumper sides carry no small codes, ticks or stencils. Favourite 32 is covered in small marks, and that density is what the brief took from it ('tactical markings all over'). It shows most at 10 m in front34, where the side behind the front wheel reads as a few big shapes with nothing small between them.
